experiment: X-ray co-crystal structure of BRD4-1 with bivalent isoquinolinone NC-III-49-1, PISA interface analysis
ph: 6.9 (protein SEC buffer; crystallization pH given in SI)
buffer: 50 mM Na/K phosphate buffer containing 2 mM DTT (final SEC purification buffer); crystallization conditions in Supplementary Tables S1–S2
construct_or_mutation: BRD4-1 (first bromodomain of human BRD4; domain boundaries not stated), N-terminal His6-TEV tag removed
other_conditions: related structures: 7MRB (monovalent NC-III-53-1 with BRD4-1); PISA interface ~340 Å2 involving 9 residues of each monomer; 0.25–2.5 mM compound, 2.5–10% DMSO; two KAc sites related by 2-fold axis
dynamics_type: ligand-induced dimerization / conformational plasticity (static crystal state)
alt_state_structure: 7LA9: inhibitor-bridged dimeric state of BRD4-1 (Fig. 4A; Accession codes)
author_claim: The bivalent inhibitor promotes and stabilizes a distinct dimeric state of BRD4-1, whose interface alone is insufficient for dimerization.
anchor: X-ray grade crystals were obtained only for BRD4–1, and structure solution revealed a dimeric state with inhibitor positioned at the protein-protein interface
locator: Results, 'Structural consequence of bivalent isoquinolinone inhibitor interaction with BRD4–1'; Fig. 4A; conditions: Experimental Section
caveat_note: Dimer observed only in crystals; no solution test for BRD4-1 (SAXS done on BRDT-T only), no exchange rates or populations. PISA low complexation significance score implies the dimer is not intrinsically stable without the bivalent ligand. Construct boundaries of BRD4-1 not stated, so residue mapping to entry is not made.

experiment: SEC-SAXS of BRDT tandem bromodomain (BRDT-T) without and with bivalent inhibitor; Guinier, p(r), ab initio DAMMIN and EOM rigid-body models
buffer: 50 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 5% v/v ethylene glycol, 2.5% v/v DMSO and 2 mM DTT
construct_or_mutation: BRDT-T (residues 2 – 416), N-terminal His6-TEV tag removed; BRDT (homolog of BRD4)
other_conditions: Rg 54 → 45 Å; Dmax 285 → 250 Å; BD1–BD2 distance ~150 Å (open) → ~45 Å (compact); Superdex 200 Increase, 0.7 mL/min
dynamics_type: open-to-compact interdomain rearrangement upon intramolecular bivalent binding
author_claim: NC-III-49-1 forms an in cis complex with BRDT-T by engaging BD1 and BD2, making the tandem domain more compact.
anchor: the radius of gyration (R g ) decreasing from 54 to 45 Å and the maximum intraparticle distance (D max ) from 285 to 250 Å.
locator: Results, 'Bivalent isoquinolinone inhibitor forms an intramolecular complex...'; Fig. 4D–G; conditions: Experimental Section, SEC-SAXS
caveat_note: BRDT-T, not BRD4; the authors say more protein/inhibitor ratios and MD are needed to separate in cis vs in trans. Only a static ensemble-average change; no rates or populations.
